definitions.SNR_T: per-sample transmission SNR of the ratio T/sigma_T, sigma_T/T = sqrt(1/SNR_atm^2 + 1/SNR_ref^2)
definitions.SNR_single_TOA: one unattenuated sample, random terms (shot + background shot + NEP)
definitions.SNR_reference: SNR_single_TOA * sqrt(n_ref), n_ref = 100 samples above 80 km
definitions.cap: systematics cap 2000 applied in quadrature after the random chain (paper convention)

solar.model: 5772-K blackbody disk (ETC) scaled to ASTM E490 at 10 um
solar.note: the paper's 2.5 uW at 8.80 um follows from the unscaled disk model; the E490-anchored value is lower by the scale factor

geometry.slit: narrow dimension = altitude = n_rows pixels = 0.1-um element width in the spectral direction; long dimension along the solar diameter (M columns)
geometry.array_format_needed: 94 spectral x 112 spatial pixels for 47 elements (a 320x240 array suffices)
geometry.diffraction_note: 2.44 lambda F/pitch; > 2 pixels means the 0.1-um element (2 pixels) is blurred by diffraction at this F-number -- a design constraint, strongest at 20.4 um

flags: Uncooled microbolometer (VOx): catalogue NEP 1e-11 W/rtHz at 17 um pitch implies D* = 1.7e8; the Appendix text quotes D* ~ 2e10, which is the radiative-exchange LIMIT of an ideal 300-K thermal detector (computed below: 1.8e10), not a measured array value; measured arrays give ~1e9 (below). The two paper numbers are therefore inconsistent by a factor ~100 and neither is the sourced value.

Uncooled thermopile array: catalogue NEP 1e-9 W/rtHz at 100 um implies D* = 1e7; the sourced MCS thermopiles are 8e8 (with readout) to 1.7e9 (detector alone) -- the catalogue was ~100x too pessimistic. The Appendix statement that the microbolometer D* is '~20 times the thermopile's' is NOT supported by the sourced values (both ~1e9).
Pyroelectric (DLaTGS): catalogue NEP 3e-10 W/rtHz at 100 um implies D* = 3.3e7; OTES/L'TES measure 1.2e9 at 10 Hz. AC-only remains true (needs modulation).

Photon detectors (InSb, HgCdTe, Si:As, Si:Sb, T2SL): NEP is derived from D* and pitch by construction, so they are self-consistent; their D* values are representative (not flight-measured here) and are flagged as such.

adopted.cooling: none; TEC stabilization of the FPA (E-THEMIS, THEMIS +/-1 mK)
adopted.basis: conservative round value of the measured range below; tau from E-THEMIS

derived_from_measurements.netd_formula: NETD = (4F^2+1) sqrt(df)/(sqrt(A_d) D* tau_o dM/dT), df = frame/2, tau_o = 1

vox_microbolometer.inconsistency_statement: Paper text D* ~2e10 = ideal-thermal-detector limit (1.8e+10); ETC catalogue 1e-11 W/rtHz at 17 um = 1.7e+08; measured arrays 8.2e+08-1.4e+09. Adopted 1e+09.

adopted.basis: OTES/L'TES measured D* 1.2e9 at 10 Hz, 22 C, single element, AC-coupled; in an FTS the moving mirror modulates the signal; a staring spectrograph would need a chopper

window_edge_tau2_parametric.note: paper: 'the 7.8-9.3 um shoulder with tau_O3 <~ 2 in the element average'; the 8.90 element reads 1.68 in the archive; tau = 2 taken as the edge case

saturation.statement: In an R~100 spectrograph each pixel receives a 0.05-um slice of the solar spectrum at the design F-number: 0.47 of a 300-K f/1 scene (the configuration in which microbolometer NETDs are measured; equivalent scene temperature 258 K), so the Sun does not saturate the array; a broadband 7.5-13.5-um imager pointed at the Sun receives 412x a 300-K scene and does saturate, which is why imagers carry a Sun flag (THEMIS). The margin depends on the gain state; no attenuator is required at the adopted parameters, but the saturation figure is a vendor parametrization, not a measured flight value.

cancelled_by_ratio: detector responsivity and electronic gain, if constant over the event
the solar spectrum itself (same disk strip, same spectral slice)
slow degradation of optics/detector between events (Chu1989)
not_cancelled: additive offsets (warm-optics emission, dark level, stray light) -- must be measured (space look before/after the event) and subtracted
nonlinearity between the TOA level and the attenuated level
gain/responsivity drift within the event (FPA temperature, 1/f noise)
pointing-dependent solar-disk structure (limb darkening) if the strip moves on the disk

offset_requirement.statement: the 300-K background on the element must be known/subtracted to this fraction of itself

nonlinearity_requirement.statement: response R(S)=S(1+e2 S/S_TOA): |e2| below this over the TOA-to-30% range; MCS thermopile spec is 1 % (Foote2003), so a 1 %-class linearity would need characterization/correction by a factor ~14

fpa_temperature_requirement.heritage: THEMIS stabilizes the IR FPA to +/-0.001 K (Christensen2004)

vertical_resolution.onion_peel: shell k is bounded by successive tangent heights z_k, z_k+1 (0.5 km apart); the retrieved shell extinction is the path-weighted average over the net response above, so the retrieval resolution is >= the 0.5-km grid and ~0.5-1 km FWHM-to-base for these terms; the onion-peel gain g = 1.097 (saimon.onion_peel) is already in K_GEOM
vertical_resolution.statement: 0.5 km is the SAMPLING; the resolution budget (FOV, smear, diffraction, pointing, retrieval response) gives ~0.5 km FWHM with a 1-km base for the adopted dwell = 0.5 km / descent rate; none of this is demonstrated -- these are the requirement-level numbers

mass_power.statement: No mass, power, thermal or duty-cycle budget exists in this analysis; the 'small-satellite class' description is an unverified design objective supported only by the flown analogues below.

table_d2_corrections.pyroelectric_row: Pyroelectric (DLaTGS) | 2--40 | ~300 K | high-R in FTS; AC-only (Mini-TES, OTES, L'TES)
table_d2_corrections.caption_ethemis: E-THEMIS on Europa Clipper (Christensen2024) flies uncooled microbolometer bands at 14--28 and 28--80 um, which demonstrates microbolometer spectral response across the long-wave bands considered here; it does not verify the SNR of a solar-occultation instrument.
table_d2_corrections.caption_photon: Among the candidates surveyed in this table, the only photon detectors reaching 20--29 um are the extrinsic-silicon devices (Si:As, Si:Sb), which need sub-10 K cooling; this is a statement about the surveyed candidates, not a survey of all photon-detector technologies.
table_d2_corrections.text_heritage: OTES and L'TES use a single uncooled DLATGS pyroelectric detector (Christensen et al. 2018, Sect. 2.3.2; Christensen et al. 2024), not thermopiles; thermopile heritage is Diviner and MCS (Paige et al. 2010; McCleese et al. 2007; Foote et al. 2003).
table_d2_corrections.text_dstar: Replace 'D* (~2e10) is ~20 times the thermopile's' by the sourced values: VOx microbolometer arrays ~1e9 cm Hz^1/2 W^-1 (NETD 30-50 mK at f/1, 17-um pitch; E-THEMIS flight NEP 4.95e-12 W at 12 um), MCS thermopiles 0.8-1.7e9, OTES/L'TES DLATGS 1.2e9 at 10 Hz; 2e10 is the ideal 300-K thermal-detector limit. The microbolometer is preferred for its staring 2-D format and ~12-ms time constant, not for a D* advantage.
